idiom_name: collection filter/filterNot/collect with predicate functions; withFilter in for-comprehensions
implementation_notes: Scala's collections supply the filter as a method taking a predicate function - `msgs.filter(_.header("type").contains("price"))` - with `filterNot` for the inverse, `collect` (a partial function) when the criterion also transforms the accepted message, and `withFilter` inside for-comprehensions to avoid intermediate collections. `Iterator` and `LazyList` keep the pipeline lazy and single-pass, which is what a streaming message feed needs. A `MessageFilter` type is warranted only when the criterion is data (an injected `Message => Boolean`) or when filters are named, composable components.
pitfalls: Iterator is exhausted after one terminal operation: a filtered Iterator cannot be reused and a second foreach silently does nothing.
Eager collections (List, Vector) allocate a copy per stage; chain with Iterator or withFilter for long feeds.
filter expects `A => Boolean`: a partial-function literal (`{ case ... }`) typechecks against collect but not against filter - a common error when adapting between them.
